# Transformer / Attention Deep-Dive

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/transformer-attention-deep-dive)

`ml-knowledge` `pytorch` `transformer`

---

## Requirements

- Derive scaled dot-product attention from fundamentals: `softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V`, including the purpose of the scaling factor and softmax.
- Describe the responsibilities of encoders and decoders, identify where masks are used, and explain when a single stack is sufficient.
- Explain multi-head attention: the reason for dividing into heads, how the parameter count works, and the trade-off involving head dimension.
- Relate the concepts to current systems: KV-cache behavior at inference, Flash Attention's memory-saving kernel, and the RoPE positional-encoding equation.

## Examples

Recent question stems:

- "Guide me through Transformer architecture. In what cases would you use only an encoder or only a decoder?"
- "What is the reason for dividing attention scores by `sqrt(d_k)`?"
- "Put the RoPE equation on the board."
- "How do Adam and AdamW differ? When would you move to SGD with momentum?"
- "Define distributed training and name the parallelism approaches (DP, TP, PP), along with when each is most effective."

## Notes

- Multiple Applied Scientist interviews directly request the mathematics (`Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)`, RoPE rotation matrix) on the board—state it exactly rather than describing it loosely.
- Hands-on follow-ups are common: "How did you apply masking in your multi-turn agent?", "What occurs when the context becomes longer than the trained position range?" Have one project example ready for every dimension.
- KV cache, Flash Attention, and RoPE frequently appear as a group, although each tackles a separate scaling problem (memory, throughput, and length generalization).
- The `1/sqrt(d_k)` factor is essential rather than decorative: when `d_k` increases, the variance of `Q·K^T` increases linearly, driving softmax toward saturation and causing gradients to disappear. Scaling by `sqrt(d_k)` maintains the pre-softmax logits near unit variance.
- Multi-head attention is more than an increase in "capacity": one head combines information from different subspaces, erasing separate relational cues (syntactic, positional, and semantic). For `h` heads with `d_k = d_model / h`, the overall parameter count matches that of one head with width `d_model`; the advantage is representational rather than parametric.
- The decoder's causal mask uses `logits.masked_fill(mask == 0, -inf)` before softmax; padding masks are applied identically over the key dimension. A one-position error is the most frequent masking bug—the position currently being processed must remain unmasked so it can attend to itself.
- At inference step `t`, the KV cache computes only the incoming `q_t`; the `K, V` values for positions `0..t-1` are stored and joined with the new `k_t, v_t`. Per request, memory scales as `O(layers × heads × seq_len × head_dim × 2)`, which determines GPU-memory planning for long-context serving.
- Flash Attention divides `Q, K, V` into SRAM-sized tiles, processes attention one block at a time with an online softmax (running maximum plus denominator), and recomputes values during backpropagation instead of storing the `(N, N)` attention matrix. The result is the same numerically, uses O(N) rather than O(N²) memory, and runs 2-4× faster in wall-clock time.
- RoPE rotates `Q` and `K` at each position within two-dimensional subspaces. Since applying the same angular difference to `q` and `k` for a fixed positional separation leaves `q·k` dependent only on the *relative* offset, it provides relative-position behavior.

## Preparation

- Build scaled dot-product attention and one Transformer block in plain PyTorch without `nn.MultiheadAttention`, and finish within 15 minutes.
- From memory, put the rotary mapping $$(x1, x2) \to (x1 \cos \theta - x2 \sin \theta, x1 \sin \theta + x2 \cos \theta)$$ on a whiteboard and explain how it retains relative position.
- Learn the Flash-Attention block-tiling idea (tile QK^T in SRAM and recompute during backward); one precise sentence is sufficient.
- Prepare a 30-second account of "my multi-turn agent did X" that can handle questions about context overflow.
- Practice in stages: (1) put the equation and the `sqrt(d_k)` rationale on the whiteboard; (2) code scaled-dot-product attention in raw PyTorch using a `(B=2, H=4, T=16, D=8)` tensor; (3) introduce a causal mask and inspect that position `t` can see only `0..t`; (4) expand it to multi-head attention with `view + transpose`; (5) attach a small KV-cache loop and verify that its step-`t` output equals the matching full-sequence forward pass.
- Learn the four scaling bottlenecks and their corresponding mechanisms: long-context memory → Flash Attention; inference-time KV memory → KV cache / MQA / GQA; generalization beyond absolute positions → RoPE / ALiBi; training throughput → tensor / sequence parallelism.
- Prepare a 30-second example for each axis ("I encountered OOM at 32k context and changed to GQA + paged KV cache"); interviewers nearly always move from theory to a project example.
